agent_lines:
Gotcha, thanks for calling in off the flyer.  

Before I dive into how it works, what kind of business do you run?

Makes sense, closing early can really mess with calls and orders.  

So when you close early now, what usually gets missed — orders, stock questions, contractor accounts, something else?

Yeah, that totally tracks for a hardware store.  

When those stock questions and orders don’t get answered, do people usually call back later, or do they just go to another store?

Yeah, that’s the real risk — they don’t tell you when they switch.  

When you think about “how this works,” are you more curious about what it actually does day-to-day, or the tech behind it?

Got it, that’s exactly where we should start.  

So… day to day, when someone calls after hours or while your team’s busy, what do you want to happen instead of voicemail?

Gotcha, so you want callers helped and captured, not just dumped to voicemail.  

And those missed stock questions and orders — any sense how many calls a week are hitting voicemail right now? 10, 20, 30?

Yeah, that’s still a decent number slipping through.  

Do you feel like most of those 15–20 a week would buy or place an order if someone actually picked up?

Yeah, totally hear you — that adds up quietly.  

Has anyone ever walked you through what that might actually be costing you each month, or not really?

Right, you just feel it leaking but haven’t put numbers to it.  

Mind if we do a super quick back-of-the-napkin math on it together?

Totally fair, just browsing is okay.  

Pricing depends on call volume and setup, and Jay walks through that live — for now, how much detail do you want on what it does day-to-day?

Makes sense, let’s keep it simple.  

Day to day, when your line rings and no one’s free or you’re closed, our system answers, helps the caller, and captures the order or message instead of voicemail. It then sends you the details so your team can follow up or prep the order.  

On the phone side, we don’t replace your carrier — we sit on top of your existing number, so calls still come to you first and only roll to us when you can’t get them.  

Does that match what you’re hoping for, or were you picturing something different with your current phone setup?

Yeah, you’re right in the sweet spot for this.  

On integration, we simply set your existing number to roll over to our line when you don’t answer or when you’re closed — no new phones or carrier change.  

On pricing, it’s based on your call volume and how many calls you want covered, not a one-size-fits-all flat rate.  

Since you’re just browsing, would it help if we just focused on integration a bit more first, or are you mainly trying to see if this could fit your budget at all?

Totally understand, thanks for being straight about that.  

Since budget’s the big piece, are you looking more for something “bare minimum to catch missed calls,” or “happy to pay a bit more if it clearly pays for itself”?

Yeah, that makes sense, start lean and let it earn its keep.  

So, it’s a simple 20‑minute walkthrough where we show exactly how many of those 15–20 missed calls we’d catch and what that means in dollars. What’s better for you to see that and talk budget properly — later this week or next week?

Totally hear you, you want to think it through first.  

Real quick though — if we could guarantee you 5 to 10 extra booked orders a month, would that be worth a 20‑minute look this week?

Yeah, I get that, you’re just not ready to take a step yet.  

Before we wrap, is it mainly timing right now, or are you unsure it would actually move the needle on those missed calls?

Gotcha, timing’s the big thing for you.  

Here’s the upside: thinking is free, but every week those 15–20 calls keep slipping. A 20‑minute walkthrough just shows the math, then you decide. Would later this week be totally out of the question, or a maybe if it’s no‑pressure?
Totally okay, thanks for walking through this with me today. If you decide you want to plug those missed calls later, just give us a ring back.
Sounds good, I’m glad it was helpful. Have a great rest of your day, and we’ll be here if you need us.
